project.name: tuck
project.description: A Go CLI dotfiles and package manager for configuring one active source registry, resolving package references, planning safe filesystem changes, applying package/file operations, rendering command output, and validating behavior through acceptance scripts.

nodes.name: Source Registry Management
nodes.summary: Manages the machine-local registry of tuck source trees and the active source used by CLI operations. It loads, normalizes, validates, persists, lists, and selects source entries so package resolution has a trusted source root.

businessRules: Source IDs must be valid and unique.
Registered source roots must be canonicalized and must not overlap in unsafe ways.
Commands operate through a single active/default source when a specific source is not supplied.
crossDomainInteractions: Provides active source context to package discovery and planning.
Passes source records to command output rendering.
Acceptance scripts verify source add/list/default behavior.

nodes.name: Package Discovery and Resolution
nodes.summary: Discovers package directories and leaves under configured source trees, parses package references, and resolves user input to concrete package identities and entries. This domain translates CLI package names and paths into source-backed package content for use, drop, show, status, and adopt workflows.

businessRules: Package references must parse into valid source/package components.
Package operations must resolve against the selected active source.
Adopt resolution uses package-to-target and target-to-package translation rules.
crossDomainInteractions: Feeds resolved package entries into planning and status workflows.
Supplies package data to output rendering.

nodes.name: Filesystem Planning and Application
nodes.summary: Builds safe plans for package and file operations, detects conflicts and privilege requirements, and applies validated mutations to the target filesystem. It is the core write path for use, drop, adopt, and eject commands.

businessRules: Filesystem changes are planned before they are applied.
Conflicts, directory blockers, and privilege requirements must be surfaced before mutation.
Apply validates each mkdir, rmdir, symlink, remove-symlink, and move action before recording changes.
crossDomainInteractions: Consumes resolved packages and target scope information.
Reports plans, conflicts, and privilege prompts through output rendering.
Status evaluation uses the same package and target relationships to classify managed files.

nodes.name: Status and Inspection
nodes.summary: Computes read-only status classifications for target files and package entries. It lets users inspect whether package content is linked, missing, changed, unmanaged, or otherwise differs from the configured source state before or after mutations.

businessRules: Status commands do not mutate files.
Status scope must expand user input into package or target paths consistently.
Package status depends on resolved package entries and active source context.
crossDomainInteractions: Uses path translation helpers shared with planning.
Publishes classifications through CLI output rendering.

nodes.name: CLI Output and Error Reporting
nodes.summary: Renders user-facing text and JSON responses for source, package, plan, status, and error outcomes. It centralizes terminal UX decisions such as envelopes, colors, nouns, privilege hints, error classification, and contextual details.

businessRules: Commands should present consistent result envelopes and human-readable summaries.
Typed application errors are classified into user-facing messages and details.
Privilege-required outcomes need explicit rendering so users understand why an apply could not proceed.
crossDomainInteractions: Consumes data from every command domain.
Receives typed errors from source, manifest, package, resolve, plan, and state layers.
Acceptance scripts verify command output contracts.

nodes.name: Acceptance Behavior Validation
nodes.summary: Runs txtar-based CLI scenarios that validate tuck behavior end to end. This domain captures the product contract for foundation, source, and package workflows by executing commands against scripted fixtures.

businessRules: Acceptance scenarios should exercise user-observable CLI behavior rather than private implementation details.
Script environments must isolate state and filesystem effects.
Foundation, source, and package suites protect the documented command contract.
crossDomainInteractions: Validates source registry, package resolution, planning, applying, status, and output domains.
Uses documentation and script fixtures as executable product specifications.

nodes.name: Add Source Record

nodes.name: List Sources

nodes.name: Render Source List

nodes.name: Dispatch Source Default
nodes.summary: The source command family routes default-source requests to the default action.

nodes.name: Load Registry
nodes.summary: Current source registry state is loaded before changing the default.

nodes.name: Find Requested Source
nodes.summary: The registry searches for the requested source ID before making it active.

nodes.name: Validate Registry

nodes.name: Persist Default Selection

nodes.name: Render Default Result

nodes.summary: The pkgref parser converts the input string into a Ref value or typed reference error.

nodes.name: Derive Active Source
nodes.summary: Resolution fills omitted source context from the active source when needed.

nodes.name: Handle Reference Error
nodes.summary: Reference and source errors are classified for user-facing output.

nodes.name: List Packages
nodes.summary: Enumerates packages available under configured source trees and renders the package list for discovery.

nodes.name: Dispatch Package List
nodes.summary: The package command family routes list requests to the package-list action.

nodes.name: Load Active Source
nodes.summary: Package listing uses the active source or explicit source context from flags.

nodes.name: List Package Roots
nodes.summary: The packages layer builds a listing from configured source roots and list options.

nodes.name: Walk Package Tree
nodes.summary: Package traversal enumerates directories and leaf packages in the source tree.

nodes.name: Render Package List
nodes.summary: The CLI renderer presents package names and counts to the user.

nodes.name: Resolve Package
nodes.summary: Resolves a package reference to concrete package identity and entries for show, use, drop, adopt, and status workflows.

nodes.name: Parse Input Reference
nodes.summary: The package reference is parsed before filesystem lookup.

nodes.name: Choose Source
nodes.summary: The active-source resolver determines which source tree should satisfy the reference.

nodes.name: Resolve Package
nodes.summary: The packages layer resolves the reference into package metadata and entries.

nodes.name: Resolve Single or Adopt Variant
nodes.summary: Specialized resolution handles single-package and adopt-specific workflows.

nodes.name: Translate Paths
nodes.summary: Path helpers translate package-relative paths to target paths and back.

nodes.summary: Resolved data is rendered for show or passed onward to planning and status.

nodes.name: Use Package
nodes.summary: Plans and optionally applies symlink and directory actions that bring a resolved package into the target root.

nodes.name: Dispatch Package Use
nodes.summary: The package command family routes use requests to the package-use action.

nodes.name: Resolve Package
nodes.summary: The packages layer resolves the requested package entries from the active source.

nodes.name: Build Use Plan
nodes.summary: The plan layer creates actions needed to link package entries into the target root.

nodes.name: Detect Conflicts
nodes.summary: Planning marks conflicts, directory blockers, and privilege requirements before mutation.

nodes.name: Render Use Plan
nodes.summary: The renderer summarizes planned package-use changes and conflicts.

nodes.name: Apply Plan
nodes.summary: When requested, validated plan actions are applied to the filesystem.

nodes.name: Drop Package
nodes.summary: Plans and optionally applies removals for package-managed symlinks and related directory cleanup.

nodes.name: Dispatch Package Drop

nodes.name: Resolve Package
nodes.summary: The selected package is resolved so managed target entries can be calculated.

nodes.name: Build Drop Plan

nodes.name: Check Privilege and Conflicts
nodes.summary: Planning detects blocked removals, conflicts, and privilege requirements.

nodes.name: Render Drop Plan
nodes.summary: The renderer presents planned drop actions and any plan errors.

nodes.name: Apply Drop Actions
nodes.summary: Validated removals and directory operations are applied when execution is requested.

nodes.name: Adopt Target

nodes.name: Dispatch Adopt
nodes.summary: The file command family routes adopt requests to the adopt action.

nodes.name: Resolve for Adopt

nodes.name: Classify Adopt Conflict

nodes.name: Render Adopt Plan
nodes.summary: The renderer presents the adopt plan or plan error details.

nodes.name: Apply Adopt Actions
nodes.summary: Validated adopt actions are applied through the common plan apply path.

nodes.name: Eject Target
nodes.summary: Plans and optionally applies operations that remove a target from tuck management while preserving or pruning filesystem state as appropriate.

nodes.name: Dispatch Eject
nodes.summary: The file command family routes eject requests to the eject action.

nodes.name: Build Eject Plan
nodes.summary: The plan layer determines whether and how the target can be ejected from management.

nodes.name: Check Managed State
nodes.summary: Eject planning emits not-managed messages when the target is not a tuck-managed link.

nodes.name: Prune After Eject
nodes.summary: Directory cleanup is planned after ejection when safe.

nodes.name: Render Eject Plan
nodes.summary: The renderer reports planned eject actions or plan errors.

nodes.name: Apply Eject Actions
nodes.summary: Validated eject and cleanup actions are applied through the common apply path.

nodes.name: Apply Plan
nodes.summary: Executes a previously built mutation plan only after validating each action against the current filesystem state.

nodes.name: Receive Planned Actions
nodes.summary: The apply function receives planned filesystem actions from use, drop, adopt, or eject planning.

nodes.name: Preflight Actions
nodes.summary: Apply preflight records expected path kinds and planned changes before mutation.

nodes.name: Validate Action
nodes.summary: Action-specific validators check mkdir, rmdir, symlink, remove-symlink, and move safety.

nodes.name: Translate Filesystem Paths
nodes.summary: Apply helpers compute filesystem paths, link paths, sources, and destinations.

nodes.name: Record Mutations
nodes.summary: Validated changes are recorded so later actions account for prior planned removals and directories.

nodes.name: Perform Mutations
nodes.summary: The filesystem operations execute after validation confirms the plan is still safe.

nodes.name: Derive Active Scope
nodes.summary: Status scope logic determines the active source and target root context.

nodes.name: Expand Input Path
nodes.summary: Input paths are expanded consistently before classification.

nodes.name: Classify File
nodes.summary: The status package classifies the target file relationship to tuck-managed source content.

nodes.name: Render Status

nodes.name: Package Status
nodes.summary: Resolves a package and classifies all relevant package entries against the target filesystem.

nodes.name: Dispatch Package Status

nodes.name: Resolve Package
nodes.summary: The requested package is resolved to package entries and identity.

nodes.name: Derive Status Scope
nodes.summary: Status scope uses active source and target root information to classify entries.

nodes.name: Classify Package
nodes.summary: The status package computes classifications for resolved package entries.

nodes.name: Convert Entries
nodes.summary: Status classifications are converted into entries ready for rendering.

nodes.name: Render Package Status
nodes.summary: The renderer presents package-level status output.

nodes.name: Render Success Output
nodes.summary: Formats successful command results for source lists, package lists, plans, and status responses in text or JSON.

nodes.name: Create Renderer
nodes.summary: The CLI creates a renderer configured for output mode and color behavior.

nodes.name: Choose Color
nodes.summary: Color support is detected or disabled before human-readable output is written.

nodes.name: Build Envelope
nodes.summary: Command data is wrapped into consistent output envelopes for JSON or text rendering.

nodes.name: Render Domain Data
nodes.summary: Specialized renderers handle sources, package lists, use plans, generic plans, and status results.

nodes.name: Write Output
nodes.summary: The renderer writes the final output to the command response stream.

nodes.name: Render Error Output
nodes.summary: Classifies typed application errors and renders actionable error messages, details, and privilege hints.

nodes.name: Receive Error
nodes.summary: Command handlers pass typed application errors from state, manifest, package, resolve, or plan layers.

nodes.name: Classify Error
nodes.summary: The renderer maps internal error kinds to user-facing classifications.

nodes.name: Derive Details
nodes.summary: Detail messages and contextual records explain what failed and why.

nodes.name: Check Privilege Hint
nodes.summary: Privilege-required plan errors are recognized for explicit user guidance.

nodes.name: Render Error
nodes.summary: The renderer writes the final error envelope or text response.

nodes.name: Select Script Suite
nodes.summary: Acceptance suite definitions choose foundation, source, and package script groups.

nodes.name: Set Up Script Environment
nodes.summary: The harness creates isolated state and filesystem context for CLI script execution.

nodes.name: Run Script Suite
nodes.summary: The harness executes the selected txtar script suite as end-to-end CLI scenarios.

nodes.name: Check Results
nodes.summary: Script expectations verify command output and filesystem effects against the product contract.

nodes.name: Validate CLI Scenarios
nodes.summary: Uses foundation, source, and package txtar fixtures as executable specifications for the command contract.

nodes.name: Load Foundation Fixtures
nodes.summary: Foundation scripts validate baseline command behavior and project setup assumptions.

nodes.name: Load Source Fixtures
nodes.summary: Source scripts validate source registry command behavior.

nodes.name: Load Package Fixtures
nodes.summary: Package scripts validate package use, listing, and related workflows.

nodes.name: Compare Output Contract
nodes.summary: Expected output in fixtures protects command rendering behavior.

nodes.name: Compare Filesystem Contract
nodes.summary: Expected filesystem state in fixtures protects planning and apply behavior.

edges.description: Active source registry state selects the source tree used to parse and resolve package references.
Resolved package identities and entries become the inputs for use, drop, adopt, and eject plans.
Planning and status share target/package path relationships so users can inspect effects before and after changes.
Status commands need active source and target root context from registry state.
Source registry commands render source records and state errors through the CLI output layer.
Package listings, resolved package displays, and package-reference errors are rendered by the output layer.
Plans, conflicts, privilege requirements, and apply errors are rendered as user-facing command output.
Status classifications are formatted by the renderer for terminal or JSON output.
Acceptance source scripts verify source registry flows.
Acceptance package scripts verify package discovery and resolution behavior.
Acceptance scripts verify planned and applied filesystem effects.
Acceptance fixtures protect the command output contract.
